paper_type_rationale: The paper proposes MINT-CoT, a trained mathematical multimodal reasoning method that inserts selected visual tokens into chain-of-thought reasoning through an Interleave Token and a three-stage SFT plus RL recipe.
dominant_domain: Mathematical multimodal reasoning, interleaved visual tokens, chain-of-thought training, token selection, reinforcement learning.
must_cover: MINT-CoT targets mathematical figure reasoning where text-only CoT and box-shaped visual regions are insufficient.
The Interleave Token selects visual tokens by comparing projected hidden states with visual token embeddings.
The dataset contains 54K mathematical problems with reasoning steps aligned to grid-indexed visual regions.
Training has three stages: text-only CoT SFT, interleaved CoT SFT, and interleaved CoT RL.
MINT-CoT-7B improves over the Qwen2-VL baseline on MathVista-Math, GeoQA, and MMStar-Math.
Ablations show that original-image interleaving is harmful and token-level selection is better than coarse alternatives.
key_numbers: MINT-CoT-7B reaches 73.70 on MathVista-Math All, compared with 41.11 for Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct baseline.
MINT-CoT-7B reaches 64.72 on GeoQA, compared with 37.80 for the baseline.
MINT-CoT-7B reaches 69.6 on MMStar-Math, compared with 46.4 for the baseline.
Stage ablation: text-only CoT SFT reaches 64.07 on MathVista-Math All, interleaved CoT SFT reaches 67.78, and interleaved CoT RL reaches 73.70.
Interleaving method ablation: original image CoT SFT drops to 40.37 on MathVista-Math All, while interleaved CoT SFT reaches 67.78.
MINT-CoT-7B outperforms the best listed open-source model by +1.11 on MathVista-Math All, +5.72 on GeoQA, and +1.2 on MMStar-Math.
real_comparisons: Compared with text-only CoT, MINT-CoT inserts visual token sets before reasoning steps.
Compared with box-shaped visual CoT, MINT-CoT can select arbitrary token shapes inside mathematical figures.
Compared with original-image interleaving, MINT-CoT avoids injecting excessive unrelated visual tokens.
Compared with PatchCue, MINT-CoT focuses on mathematical visual token alignment rather than general patch-bbox cues.

central_claims.claim: Interleave Token based visual token selection improves mathematical multimodal reasoning.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The method and main tables show large improvements over the Qwen2-VL baseline on mathematical subsets.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove that the selected visual tokens are always causally necessary for every answer.

central_claims.claim: The three-stage training strategy is necessary for strong performance.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Stage ablation shows text-only SFT, interleaved SFT, and RL each adds performance on key benchmarks.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not fully separate the effects of dataset quality and objective design.

central_claims.claim: Fine-grained token selection is better than simply inserting the original image at every reasoning step.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Original-image CoT SFT performs much worse than interleaved token selection on MathVista-Math.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not rule out stronger retrieval or attention-based image reinsertion methods.

claim_boundaries: The paper is focused on mathematical visual reasoning, not general open-world VQA.
The dataset construction uses GPT-4o, PaddleOCR, and grid-indexed images.
The reported gains are strongest against the authors' Qwen2-VL baseline.
The paper evaluates selected mathematical subsets rather than every ability axis of the benchmarks.
negative_or_limiting_results: Original-image CoT SFT drops MathVista-Math All to 40.37, below text-only CoT SFT.
Bounding Box CoT SFT is below Interleaved CoT SFT on GeoQA and MathVista-Math All.
TQA is not the strongest subtask for MINT-CoT; it matches but does not exceed the baseline after final RL.
Several appendix figure/table crops were partial and are transcribed rather than used as primary images.
mechanism_result_map: Interleave Token similarity maps to arbitrary-shaped token selection inside math figures.
Grid images and OCR maps to token-index annotations for mathematical symbols and regions.
Text-only CoT SFT maps to learning the reasoning format before visual interleaving.
Interleaved CoT SFT maps to learning visual token insertion and alignment.
Interleaved CoT RL maps to additional gains from answer-level optimization.
comparative_positioning: MINT-CoT is a Train-line counterpart to ICoT and DaP-ICoT, but it learns visual token insertion from data.
Compared with PatchCue, MINT-CoT uses token-level selection for math figures instead of patch-bbox cue labels.
Compared with Qwen-LA, it inserts visual tokens before reasoning steps rather than at reflection moments.
Compared with DeepEyes, it relies on structured supervised data instead of emergent active perception.
reuse_takeaways: For 3D agents, define interleave tokens over view tokens, point tokens, or object tokens rather than raw pixels.
Original-image reinsertion can add noise; selection must be sparse and step-specific.
Stage-wise training is useful when the final behavior combines reasoning style and visual alignment.
Math-like 3D tasks may need symbol-region alignment before RL.
followup_questions: How robust is the Interleave Token threshold across different visual encoders?
Would diversity-aware token selection improve over simple similarity thresholding?
Can the 54K dataset construction be reproduced without GPT-4o?
Would causal removal of selected tokens reduce accuracy in the predicted reasoning step?

section_plan.focus: Explain why mathematical diagrams need step-specific visual evidence beyond text-only CoT and box-shaped regions.
Cover the 54K MINT-CoT dataset, grid indexing, OCR, keyword extraction, and visual index annotation.
Describe Interleave Token similarity scoring, visual token insertion, SFT objectives, and GRPO objective.
Report MathVista-Math, GeoQA, MMStar-Math, stage ablation, and interleaving method ablation.
Interpret MINT-CoT as step-level visual token routing for math symbols and geometry relations.
Discuss task narrowness, generated dataset dependence, selected-subset evaluation, and visual-token causality gaps.
